info.title: xRocket Pay API
info.description:
You can download the specification in OpenAPI 3.0 JSON format .

The API is based on the @xRocket payment system (@xrocket_testnet_bot for testnet).

The page is fully interactive. Provide the JWT API token you received in Authorize on the right, and you will be able to try all API methods by clicking buttons and filling in forms.

Application settings

To work with this API, your app version must be set to Current.

To change the API version for your app:

xRocket Pay → Create an app / Select app → Settings → API Version

If the app is still on Legacy, opening the API Version setting shows the webhook secret the app will use on Current.

After switching to Current, the webhook secret can be found in the bot:

xRocket Pay → Create an app / Select app → Settings → Webhook Token

To get a token for interacting with the API:

xRocket Pay → Create an app / Select app → Settings → API Token → Regenerate Token → Confirm

API Authentication

The API token is a JWT and must be passed in every request in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

To obtain a token, you must first set the app version to Current in the bot:

xRocket Pay → Create an app / Select app → Settings → API Version

after which you can get the JWT token:

xRocket Pay → Create an app / Select app → Settings → API Token → Regenerate Token → Confirm

Webhooks

Apps on the Legacy API used the Rocket-Pay-Signature header, which has been replaced by the headers described below.

For apps set to Current, webhooks contain three headers:

  • Signature-Timestamp — Unix timestamp in milliseconds, corresponding to the time the webhook was sent.

  • Signature-Version — signature scheme version. Current static value: v1.

  • Signature — hexadecimal representation of the HMAC-SHA-256 signature.

The signature is computed based on the string (it is recommended to take the request body as-is, in string form):

{Signature-Timestamp}.{request body}

The webhook secret of your app is used as the secret key without any transformations.

Important when migrating from the Legacy API

The old webhook secret from the Legacy API is not valid for apps set to Current and must be updated.

Before switching to Current, make sure your app already supports handling webhooks with the new signature scheme.

Make sure to support the updated authentication scheme when interacting with the API.

id.description: Unique webhook delivery id, can be used by the receiver for idempotency

data.description:
Webhook payload. Use the event field to determine the payload structure:
- invoice_status_changed — invoice transitioned to a new status (active → paid, expired, cancelled, ...); no payment field.
- payment_status_changed — a payment was received or its status changed; includes the payment field and the updated invoice.

When a payment completes an invoice, both events are emitted (payment_status_changed and invoice_status_changed). Delivery is best-effort in queue order, but **order is not guaranteed**: retries on a failed delivery move it later in the queue, so invoice_status_changed can arrive before payment_status_changed. Treat each event independently and dedupe by the top-level id.

Recommendations:
- Track successful payments by event = payment_status_changed AND payment.status = paid.
- Track invoice completion by event = invoice_status_changed AND invoice.status = paid.
- Determine payment finality by payment.finalizedAt != null, not by a specific status value.
- Dedupe by the top-level webhook id (stable across retries).
- Ignore unknown events and statuses — the lists may be extended without notice.
